A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TWIN/FGVQA research. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM training and evaluation results, ablations, encoder probing and human evaluation in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds benchmark evaluations and an in-context-learning comparison in appendix Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: TWIN construction, the binary correctness reward, end-to-end GRPO training and the Qwen2.5-VL 3B/InternVL3.5 1B models are unchanged (Section 3; Appendix C). The added in-context-learning experiment evaluates a comparator.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds monument doppelganger detection, shape/color-sensitivity queries from VLMs Eye and CUTE queries assessing photometric variation. This is a focused extension of perceptual test coverage; the original training, FGVQA, general-VQA, text-QA and probing datasets remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-VL 3B with in-context examples as a comparator to TWIN post-training (Appendix E.2, Table 9). v1's FGVQA comparisons use no in-context examples. Existing model baselines and the SFT-versus-RL comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify 500 CUTE pairwise queries and yes/no shape/color queries. The ICL experiment randomly supplies one positive and one negative TWIN pair per FGVQA query. These are added protocols; the original splits, metrics and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds targeted tests of robustness to confusing monuments, shape/color differences and photometric variation, and tests whether in-context prompting can substitute for post-training. The existing hard-negative, scaling, SFT/RL and encoder-probing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The four-annotator averaging in Appendix A.3 is unchanged, and the new appendix tables continue reporting point estimates only.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports base/+TWIN scores of 50.8/55.2 for Doppelgangers, 56.8/95.7 for shape, 96.1/99.7 for color and 58.8/68.0 for CUTE. Table 9 adds ICL results averaging 39.5%, compared with the retained +TWIN mean of 67.0%. Existing Tables 1–7 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The instance/task definitions and Appendix C.1 reward, advantage and GRPO objective equations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: TWIN, FGVQA, improved fine-grained perception and cross-domain transfer, preserved general capabilities and the importance of scale. The new evaluations support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly explains the existing 1.2-point InternVL INQUIRE decline through increased reliance on visual comparisons, which can fail under difficult lighting or occlusion. Appendix E.2 also discusses image-order confusion and ignored demonstrations as possible reasons for weak ICL performance.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly discloses approximately 140 hours on four A100 GPUs for one epoch of Qwen2.5-VL 3B post-training. This adds runtime information; the previously documented hardware, hyperparameters and code/data/model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds three cited works supporting the new benchmarks: Doppelgangers, Are These the Same Apple?, and VLM's Eye Examination. Existing research positioning and comparisons with Birds-to-Words and SpotTheDiff remain substantively unchanged; the latter move from Appendix E to F.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Appendix E with two evaluation subsections, expands Appendices C.1 and D, and renumbers the prior dataset-comparison section as F. Main-text editing is limited to small wording and spelling corrections, with no extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds result Tables 8–9 and renumbers the unchanged hyperparameter tables as 10–11. Existing appendix figures are regrouped across pages, including Figures 8–11. Main-text displays and the original visual examples remain substantively unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional robustness tests and ICL comparison provide useful validation beyond v1, while the new discussion addresses the previously unexplained INQUIRE regression and discloses training cost. These improve empirical support and transparency without changing the core contribution. The gains are limited by sparse detail and absent uncertainty estimates for the new evaluations.
